svg.title: How an LCW run goes. You say what you want. 1 Brainstorm, with you: Recalls earlier runs here: what you asked for and decided; Clarifies what you really mean; Tests your assumptions and what can be built; Acts like a senior partner, asking the hard questions; Ensures mutual understanding with mocks and diagrams. 2 Spec: Spec built by AI for AI, as a machine translation of your intent; The blind reviewer never sees the brainstorm; Meanwhile, probes map the code for the plan. 3 Plan: Tasks in a milestone run in parallel; Milestones run sequentially; Each check runs on Sonnet or Opus, by how risky its part is. 4 Build: Orchestrators drive the goals to completion, unblocking workers and deciding; Comes to you only if what you agreed cannot be built; Blind reviewers raise every concern, and the orchestrator decides; Work pauses by default at 75% weekly usage, or runs up to the % you explicitly allow. 5 Review: Reviewers raise every concern, earlier decisions included; The orchestrator decides what to change and what to accept. 6 Ship. Claude does stages 2 to 6 autonomously, and you review the draft pull request. A Fable advisor, a stronger model, reviews the work at every stage. In Brainstorm, cheap probes check the facts. In Spec, a blind reviewer reads only the spec and describes the intent in its own words, the orchestrator compares that with the brainstorm, and a feasibility reviewer checks every requirement can be built. The plan groups small tasks into milestones, and for very large work gives each area its own orchestrator. In Build, workers build a milestone, a blind reviewer on Sonnet or Opus checks its code without the spec, and the context is compacted, then the next milestone starts. In Review, a fresh reviewer on Sonnet or Opus, chosen by risk, checks each group of up to four requirements against the spec. Reviewers raise every concern and the orchestrator decides what to change. Context is also compacted automatically after Spec, after Plan, after Build and after Review. In Ship, the orchestrator writes the draft pull request from the brainstorm, the spec and the ledger, in three short sections with pictures: what was built, why, and how. After them it lists only what you really need to know before merging. The records of each run are kept in the folder ~/.lcw, outside your repository, so they survive compaction: brainstorm.md, spec.md, plan.md, a ledger of every decision and why, and artifacts such as mocks. The pull request lists only the decisions you would act on; the ledger keeps them all. A later brainstorm reads the records of earlier runs in the same repository, so it remembers what you asked for and decided.
svg.text: a stronger model that sees the whole conversation
Claude consults it at every stage: before a big step, when stuck, and before calling anything done.
